newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says two Chinese ships seen off Spratlys.
newsitem.headline: Manila says two Chinese ships seen off Spratlys.

text.p: The Philippines has spotted two Chinese ships, apparently survey and research vessels, near islands claimed by both China and Manila in the disputed Spratly Islands, Defence Secretary Renato de Villa said on Tuesday.
De Villa, who visited the Spratlys area last week, did not say when the vessels were seen but dismissed suggestions that Manila should file an immediate protest with Beijing.

The Spratlys are a cluster of about 190 potentially oil-rich but mostly barren isles, shoals and reefs in the South China Sea claimed wholly or in part by China, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia and Brunei.
"(The ships) are...in the vicinity of two of the islands that we have occupied," de Villa told reporters. "We are not certain, but they look like survey and research vessels."

Military sources said the ships were seen near Kota and Panata islands about half way between Pagasa, the biggest island occupied by the Philippines in the Spratlys, and Mischief Reef, which Manila also claims but that the Chinese have occupied.
Tension flared between Manila and Beijing in 1995 when President Fidel Ramos accused the Chinese of building what he said looked like naval support structures on Mischief Reef.
Beijing said they were shelters for fishermen and has refused to dismantle them.
"In the past they have been visiting this (area)," de Villa said, referring to the islands near where the latest sightings were made. "Sometimes they go to Panganiban (Mischief) Reef."

Asked if Manila was filing a protest with Beijing over the presence of the two vessels, de Villa said: "No, you don't do that automatically... I am not saying that that is not abnormal but I'm saying that there is a report to that effect. We are not recommending right away a protest as you would suggest."
The Philippines has agreed on a code of conduct separately with China and Vietnam under which they agree to exercise self-restraint and not use force in resolving the Spratlys row.
